subject: selective
title: How the writing task is marked

scenes.heading: How the writing task is marked
scenes.sub: Know what the marker wants before you write
scenes.say: In the writing section there are no options to choose. A real person reads your piece. So what are they looking for? Let's find out, so every minute you spend earns marks.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A cooking judge checks taste, look, method and cleanliness
scenes.science: A writing marker checks ideas, structure, language and accuracy
scenes.breaks: a dish is judged in seconds; your writing is read line by line, so small errors keep showing up.
scenes.say: Think of a cooking show. The judge doesn't just taste the food. They check how it looks, how it was made and how clean the bench is. A writing marker is similar: they check your ideas, your structure, your language and your accuracy.

scenes.heading: The four marking areas
points: Ideas: interesting and on the prompt
scenes.say: Here are the four areas. Ideas: is it interesting, and does it answer the prompt? Structure: is it organised, with an opening, paragraphs and an ending? Language: are the words precise and the sentences varied? Accuracy: are the spelling, punctuation and grammar correct?

scenes.heading: A 25-minute task
scenes.say: Now your time. For a twenty-five minute task, plan for about five minutes, write for about seventeen, and save three minutes to check. Five, seventeen, three.

scenes.heading: Which area loses marks?
scenes.question: A lively story for "The Locked Gate" is one 400-word block with no paragraphs. Which area loses most?
lines: Ideas: exciting and on the prompt
scenes.say: Try this. A lively story for The Locked Gate is one big block with no paragraphs. Ideas are fine. Language is fine. Accuracy isn't the issue. With no paragraphs, the piece isn't organised, so the answer is structure.

scenes.heading: Finished beats fancy
scenes.say: Remember: finished beats fancy. A long piece with no ending loses structure marks, and rushing adds errors. A shorter piece with a clear ending that you have checked covers all four areas.

points: Keep the prompt at the centre
scenes.say: Quick recap. Remember ISLE: ideas, structure, language, errors. Keep the prompt at the centre. Plan, write, then check. And finished beats fancy. Now try the practice questions!
